```{r}
#| label: setup
# The report never retypes a result. It reads the files comparison/run.R writes
# (comparison/export/r/*.csv) and the two sides' export contracts. The functions in
# comparison/R/ are sourced so the folds can show their code, and so a few lines below
# can recompute the main estimate from the contracts and check it against the export.
for (f in list.files("../R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f, keep.source = TRUE)
root <- comparison_root()
ex <- read_exports(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r"))   # R/site.R
k  <- read_contracts(root)                                          # R/contract.R
ep <- ex$endpoints; en <- ex$ends; br <- ex$bridge; inp <- ex$inputs
own <- en[en$horizon_setting == "own", ]
ea <- own[own$output == "a", ]; eb <- own[own$output == "b", ]
epv <- function(id, col = "value") ep[[col]][ep$endpoint_id == id]
steps <- bridge_steps()
# Money in running text: a dollar sign in markdown starts a formula, so escape it.
usd <- function(x, d = 1, signed = FALSE) gsub("$", "\\$", money(x, d, signed), fixed = TRUE)
# Two pandoc traps in raw HTML tables: a bare dollar sign can pair with the next one into
# a formula across cells, and "(a)" in a cell reads as a list marker that leaves the
# surrounding <div> unclosed. Every table writes both as HTML entities.
ent <- function(x) gsub("\\(([a-z])\\)", "&#40;\\1)", gsub("$", "&#36;", x, fixed = TRUE))
show <- function(df) {
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) if (is.character(x)) ent(x) else x)
  names(df) <- ent(names(df))
  knitr::kable(df, format = "html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"')
}
# Blank lines around the table, so pandoc sees the closing </div> as its own block.
scroll <- function(x) cat('\n<div class="table-scroll">\n\n', x, "\n\n</div>\n\n", sep = "")

# The code a reader sees when unfolding an exhibit: the source of the R functions that
# compute it (read from comparison/R/ at render time, so it cannot drift) and of their
# Python twins in comparison/py/bridge.py (same names).
rdef <- function(fn) {
  f <- get(fn, envir = globalenv()); sr <- attr(f, "srcref")
  l <- as.character(sr); l[1] <- paste0(fn, " <- ", l[1])
  c(sprintf("# comparison/R/%s, lines %d-%d", basename(attr(sr, "srcfile")$filename),
            as.integer(sr)[1], as.integer(sr)[3]), l, "")
}
pydef <- function(fn) {
  l <- readLines("../py/bridge.py", warn = FALSE); i <- grep(paste0("^def ", fn, "\\("), l)
  if (length(i) != 1) return(NULL)
  nxt <- which(seq_along(l) > i & grepl("^[^[:space:]#]", l))
  j <- if (length(nxt)) nxt[1] - 1 else length(l)
  while (j > i && (!nzchar(trimws(l[j])) || grepl("^#", l[j]))) j <- j - 1
  c(sprintf("# comparison/py/bridge.py, lines %d-%d (read-only display)", i, j), l[i:j], "")
}
twin_html <- function(what, r, py) {
  if (is.null(py)) {
    cat(sprintf('\n<details class="code-fold"><summary>R code for %s</summary>\n\n', what),
        "```r\n", paste(r, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n\n</details>\n\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  cat(sprintf('\n<details class="twin code-fold"><summary><a href="#" class="lang on" data-lang="r">R</a> or <a href="#" class="lang" data-lang="py">Python</a> code for %s</summary>\n\n', what),
      "::: {.lang-r}\n```r\n", paste(r, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n:::\n\n",
      "::: {.lang-py}\n```python\n", paste(py, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n:::\n\n</details>\n\n", sep = "")
}
# One fold, one line: "R or Python code for <exhibit>"; the R functions and their twins.
twin_fold <- function(exhibit, fns, py = fns) {
  r <- unlist(lapply(fns, rdef))
  p <- unlist(lapply(py, pydef))
  if (!is.null(p)) p <- c("# The Python twin (comparison/py/bridge.py); it writes comparison/export/py/.", "", p)
  twin_html(exhibit, r, p)
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_html("the setup",
  grep("^#\\|", knitr::knit_code$get("setup"), value = TRUE, invert = TRUE),
  c("# The page is built with R, so the Python twin has no setup here: it runs on its own.",
    "# From the repository root (Python 3.11 with scipy):",
    "#",
    "#   python3 comparison/py/bridge.py      # writes comparison/export/py/",
    "#",
    "# export/py/ holds the same tables this report reads from export/r/, and",
    "# comparison/tests/testthat/test-parity.R checks every number against R's to 1e-9.",
    "import pandas as pd",
    "ends = pd.read_csv(\"comparison/export/py/ends.csv\")   # the two ends of every bridge"))
```

## Introduction

::: {.report-intro}
![](assets/opa/opa-details.png){.opa-figure}

California's Proposition 40, the Billionaire Tax Act, would tax California's billionaires
once, at 5% of their net worth, paid over five years. Two analyses estimate it. The
[BSZ report](../../bsz-analysis/site/) (Boll, Saez and Zucman, NBER WP 35218, with the GGSS
expert report by Galle, Gamage, Saez and Shanske) estimates the revenue at about
**`r usd(epv("ggss_headline"), 0)`**. The [RJKDC report](../../rjkdc-analysis/site/) (Rauh,
Jaros, Kearney, Doran and Cosso) estimates a net present value for the state of
**`r usd(epv("rauh_nber_npv", "printed_value"))`** in its latest version (Jaros and Rauh,
NBER c15504, September 2026). The two numbers answer different questions, so neither can be
read against the other directly. This report puts both on one common output and walks from
one to the other, one disputed input at a time.

This report is part of the comparison's Open Policy Analysis (OPA):

- **Open Output**: [the bridge](../../index.html#the-bridge) on the overview page, where the
  output, the step sizes and the loss horizon can be switched
- **Open Analysis**: this document
- **Open Materials**: [the repository folder](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/tree/main/comparison), every script, test and data file (guide: [the materials page](materials.html))
:::

**The main estimate** is the gap on the common output (a), the gross one-time wealth tax
revenue, between the bridge's two ends: BSZ Table 5 row 1 at
`r usd(ea$bsz_model)` and the expected revenue in the NBER Monte Carlo at
`r usd(ea$nber_own)`. The gap is **`r usd(ea$bsz_model - ea$nber_own)`**. The arithmetic is in
[The main estimate](#the-main-estimate).

**Neither side reports this number.** It is this OPA's reconciliation. Each side keeps its
own main estimate on its own overview page. What this report adds is one definition both
can be estimated on, and an accounting of the distance between them.

**What "reproduced" means here.** The comparison does not re-run either side. It reads each
side's *export contract*: two files, `inputs.csv` and `outputs.csv`, that each side's own
pipeline writes under `export/r/` for others to read. It also reads a short list of values
transcribed from the PDFs with their page (`comparison/data/`). From these it rebuilds both
ends with one estimating function and checks each end against the number its authors print.

### How to read this report

Every number in running text is computed when this page is rendered, from the files
`comparison/run.R` writes. Open any "code" fold to see the R functions behind an exhibit and
their Python twins. Page numbers are PDF pages. "Shapley value" is defined where it is first
used, in [The bridge](#the-bridge).

# The common output, and what each side reports {#the-common-output}

The BSZ report says how much the one-time tax collects. The RJKDC report says what the state
gains or loses in present value once income tax lost to billionaires who leave is subtracted.
Before any step of a bridge means anything, both are put on the same two outputs:

- **(a) gross revenue**: the one-time wealth tax collected.
- **(b) net fiscal effect**: (a), plus extra income tax from assets sold to pay the tax,
  minus the present value of income tax lost to departures over a horizon of H years.

The horizon H is itself disputed. The BSZ report counts the losses for about the
`r fmt_input("H", inp$supporting_value[inp$input == "H"])` of payments (BSZ PDF p.27). The
RJKDC report counts them forever. Discounting uses the RJKDC report's own range, a rate
drawn uniformly between `r pct(pick(k$rjkdc$inputs, "rauh_mc_r_min"), 1)` and
`r pct(pick(k$rjkdc$inputs, "rauh_mc_r_max"), 1)` (Rauh p.20 eq.24). The BSZ report takes no
position on the rate.

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the four estimates on the common output", c("score_common", "rauh_ssrn_expectation", "rauh_nber_expectation", "expected_annuity"))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
d <- k$docs
dv <- function(id) as.numeric(d$value[d$input_id == id])
tab <- data.frame(
  Estimate = c("GGSS expert report (20 Jul 2026)", "BSZ NBER WP 35218, Table 5 row 1 (Aug 2026)",
               "Rauh et al., SSRN 6340778 (17 Mar 2026)", "Jaros and Rauh, NBER c15504 (Sep 2026)"),
  `(a) gross revenue` = c(money(epv("ggss_headline"), 0), money(ea$bsz_model, 1),
                          money(ea$rauh_own, 2), money(ea$nber_own, 1)),
  `(b) net fiscal effect` = c("not computed", money(eb$bsz_model, 1), money(eb$rauh_own, 2), money(eb$nber_own, 2)),
  `What the authors print` = c(
    sprintf("%s estimate, rounded to %s (p.4)", money(epv("ggss_scoring", "printed_value"), 0), money(epv("ggss_headline"), 0)),
    sprintf("%s revenue (PDF p.39); no net figure", money(epv("bsz_tab5_row1", "printed_value"), 0)),
    sprintf("mean NPV %s (p.20); revenue 'about %s' (p.14)", money(epv("rauh_ssrn_npv", "printed_value"), 1), money(dv("rauh_headline_revenue"), 0)),
    sprintf("mean NPV %s; revenue 'approximately %s' (p.1)", money(epv("rauh_nber_npv", "printed_value"), 1), money(dv("nber_headline_revenue"), 0))),
  check.names = FALSE)
scroll(show(tab))
```

Output (b) for the BSZ report is not printed by either paper. It is Table 5 row 1's own three
columns combined here: the `r usd(ea$bsz_model)` revenue, plus
`r usd(ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == "X_bsz"], 2)` of extra income tax from asset sales, minus
`r usd(ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == "PV_bsz_own"], 2)`, the present value of five years of
its income tax loss. For the RJKDC report, both outputs are the expectations of the
authors' own Monte Carlo, computed exactly rather than by drawing.

# The two ends, estimated on it {#the-two-ends}

One estimating function, `score_common()`, takes every disputed input as an argument. Each
argument takes either the BSZ report's value or the RJKDC report's. At the all-BSZ setting
the function must return BSZ Table 5 row 1. At the all-RJKDC setting it must return the
expectation of Rauh's SSRN Monte Carlo. The NBER version is then one further step. The table
checks each end against the number its authors print.

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the endpoint checks", c("bridge_inputs", "score_common"))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
e2 <- ep[ep$endpoint_id != "bsz_net_constructed", ]
scroll(show(data.frame(
  End = esc(e2$description),
  `Computed here` = vapply(e2$value, function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 3), ""),
  `Printed` = ifelse(is.na(e2$printed_value), "not printed", formatC(e2$printed_value, format = "f", digits = 1)),
  Where = ifelse(is.na(e2$printed_where), "", e2$printed_where),
  `Difference` = ifelse(is.na(e2$abs_diff_printed), "", formatC(e2$abs_diff_printed, format = "f", digits = 3)),
  check.names = FALSE)))
```

Every difference is a rounding of the printed number. The NBER mean NPV is the expectation
of the Monte Carlo (`r usd(eb$nber_own, 2)`), while the authors print one run of it
(`r usd(epv("rauh_nber_npv", "printed_value"))`).

## The main estimate {#the-main-estimate}

```{r}
bi  <- bridge_inputs(k)                       # the two input vectors, from the contracts
sup <- bi$sup
v_sup <- score_common(sup)                    # the BSZ end
oi <- k$rjkdc$inputs
nber <- rauh_nber_expectation(wt_min = 0, wt_max = pick(oi, "nber_ceiling_hardcoded"),
                              f_min = pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_min"), f_max = pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_max"),
                              c_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min"), c_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max"),
                              r_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), r_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max"))
gap <- v_sup[["a"]] - nber[["a"]]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v_sup[["a"]], ea$bsz_model)), isTRUE(all.equal(nber[["a"]], ea$nber_own)))
```

**Step 1: the BSZ end.** At the all-BSZ inputs, output (a) is the tax rate times the base,
less the avoidance allowance. The base is the `r usd(sup$W_core + sup$W_noncit, 0)` that
Forbes lists for California's billionaires on 1 July 2026, the non-US-citizen residents
(`r usd(sup$W_noncit, 0)`) included. The BSZ report applies no real-estate deduction, no
departures before the tax and no mobility response to a one-time tax. So
(a) = `r pct(sup$tau)` &times; `r usd(sup$W_core + sup$W_noncit, 0)` &times;
(1 &minus; `r pct(sup$alpha)`) = **`r usd(v_sup[["a"]], 3)`**, which is BSZ Table 5 row 1
(printed `r usd(epv("bsz_tab5_row1", "printed_value"), 0)`, PDF p.39).

**Step 2: the NBER end.** In the Monte Carlo of Jaros and Rauh's NBER version the revenue is
drawn uniformly between zero and `r usd(pick(oi, "nber_ceiling_hardcoded"), 0)`. Its
expectation is the midpoint: **`r usd(nber[["a"]], 1)`**. The authors print the revenue as
"approximately `r usd(dv("nber_headline_revenue"), 0)`" (p.1); the bridge uses the
expectation because it is the revenue the printed mean NPV assumes.

**Step 3: the gap.** `r usd(v_sup[["a"]], 3)` &minus; `r usd(nber[["a"]], 1)` =
**`r usd(gap, 3)`**, shown as `r usd(gap)`.

**Step 4: where the gap comes from.** The next section splits it into one step per disputed
input (`r usd(sum(br$shapley[br$horizon_setting == "own" & br$output == "a"]), 2, TRUE)` in
total), a model difference from the RJKDC report's rounded literals
(`r usd(ea$rauh_residual, 4, TRUE)`) and the NBER revision
(`r usd(ea$nber_step, 2, TRUE)`). The three add up to `r usd(-gap, 3)`.

```{r}
b_a <- br[br$horizon_setting == "own" & br$output == "a", ]
stopifnot(abs(sum(b_a$shapley) + ea$rauh_residual + ea$nber_step + gap) < 1e-9)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the main estimate", c("bridge_inputs", "score_common", "rauh_nber_expectation"))
```

# The bridge, step by step {#the-bridge}

Each step switches one input from the BSZ value to the RJKDC value. Because the inputs
interact (a departure matters more when the base is larger), the size of a step depends on
the order in which the inputs are switched. The report shows two answers:

- **Shapley values** (the default on the overview page). Each step's switch is averaged over
  all `r format(factorial(nrow(steps)), big.mark = ",")` orders of the
  `r nrow(steps)` steps. The code computes this exactly, by estimating the model at every one
  of the `r format(2^nrow(steps), big.mark = ",")` subsets of switched inputs. The steps then
  add up to the total gap whatever order they are read in.
- **One order**: a single sequence, the one Hoopes (2026) reads in (see
  [below](#the-hoopes-comparison)).

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the bridge tables and the figure", c("switch_inputs", "shapley_bridge", "sequential_bridge"))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
bt <- function(o) {
  b <- br[br$horizon_setting == "own" & br$output == o, ]
  b <- b[match(steps$step_id, b$step_id), ]
  ii <- inp[match(b$step_id, inp$step_id), ]
  e <- own[own$output == o, ]
  rows <- data.frame(
    Step = esc(b$title), `DISPUTES row` = b$disputes_row, Kind = b$kind,
    `BSZ value` = mapply(fmt_input, ii$input, ii$supporting_value),
    `RJKDC value` = mapply(fmt_input, ii$input, ii$rauh_value),
    Shapley = vapply(b$shapley, money, "", digits = 2, signed = TRUE),
    `One order` = vapply(b$sequential, money, "", digits = 2, signed = TRUE),
    check.names = FALSE)
  extra <- data.frame(
    Step = c("Sum of the steps", "Model difference (rounded literals)", "NBER revision"),
    `DISPUTES row` = "", Kind = c("", "model", "guesswork + data"), `BSZ value` = "", `RJKDC value` = "",
    Shapley = c(money(sum(b$shapley), 2, TRUE), money(e$rauh_residual, 4, TRUE), money(e$nber_step, 2, TRUE)),
    `One order` = c(money(sum(b$sequential), 2, TRUE), money(e$rauh_residual, 4, TRUE), money(e$nber_step, 2, TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE)
  top <- data.frame(Step = sprintf("<b>BSZ end, (%s)</b>", o), `DISPUTES row` = "", Kind = "", `BSZ value` = "",
                    `RJKDC value` = "", Shapley = money(e$bsz_model, 2), `One order` = money(e$bsz_model, 2), check.names = FALSE)
  bot <- data.frame(Step = sprintf("<b>NBER end, (%s)</b>", o), `DISPUTES row` = "", Kind = "", `BSZ value` = "",
                    `RJKDC value` = "", Shapley = money(e$nber_own, 2), `One order` = money(e$nber_own, 2), check.names = FALSE)
  scroll(show(rbind(top, rows, extra, bot)))
}
cat("\n**Output (a), gross revenue, each side's own horizon.**\n\n"); bt("a")
cat("\n**Output (b), net fiscal effect, each side's own horizon.** The horizon step switches from the BSZ report's 5 years to a perpetuity.\n\n"); bt("b")
```

Reading the (a) table: the three largest Shapley steps are
```{r}
#| results: asis
top3 <- b_a[order(b_a$shapley), ][1:3, ]
cat(paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", tolower(top3$title), usd(top3$shapley, 1, TRUE)), collapse = "; "), ".", sep = "")
```
One step raises the number: the RJKDC report applies no avoidance allowance beyond migration,
so dropping the BSZ report's `r pct(sup$alpha)` adds `r usd(b_a$shapley[b_a$step_id == "avoidance"], 1, TRUE)`.
Order matters most for estimating the one-time tax as a permanent 5-percentage-point rate:
`r usd(b_a$shapley[b_a$step_id == "one_time_as_permanent"], 1, TRUE)` averaged over all
orders, `r usd(b_a$sequential[b_a$step_id == "one_time_as_permanent"], 1, TRUE)` in the one
order shown.

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the waterfall", "build_series", py = character(0))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-waterfall
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "Output (a), Shapley steps, each side's own horizon: the same bars as the overview page's default view."
library(ggplot2)
B <- build_series(ex, "Model difference")$own$a$shapley
run <- 0; rows <- list()
for (i in seq_along(B)) {
  b <- B[[i]]
  if (b$type == "total") { y0 <- 0; y1 <- b$value; run <- b$value } else { y0 <- run; y1 <- run + b$value; run <- y1 }
  rows[[i]] <- data.frame(i = i, short = b$short, y0 = y0, y1 = y1,
                          fill = if (b$type == "total") "an estimate" else if (b$type == "model") "model difference or rounding"
                                 else if (b$value >= 0) "step that raises it" else "step that lowers it")
}
wf <- do.call(rbind, rows)
ggplot(wf) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = i - 0.38, xmax = i + 0.38, ymin = pmin(y0, y1), ymax = pmax(y0, y1), fill = fill)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("an estimate" = "#5b6873", "model difference or rounding" = "#a8b2bb",
                               "step that raises it" = "#1f6fce", "step that lowers it" = "#eb6834"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = wf$i, labels = wf$short) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "$ billion") + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

# Which of Rauh's revenue numbers is output (a)? {#which-revenue}

The RJKDC report's SSRN version prints four different revenue figures. The bridge takes the
one consistent with its `r usd(epv("rauh_ssrn_npv", "printed_value"))` headline, the expected
revenue in the same Monte Carlo, because it is the revenue that headline assumes. Using any
of the others would add a further step of the size shown.

twin_fold("the candidates", "build_all")
```

scroll(show(data.frame(
  Candidate = paste0(esc(an$label), ifelse(an$default, " (used)", "")),
  Value = vapply(an$value, money, "", digits = 2), Where = esc(an$where),
  `Extra step vs the bridge end` = vapply(an$value - an$value[an$default], function(z) if (abs(z) < 1e-9) "none" else money(z, 2, TRUE), ""),
  check.names = FALSE)))
```

# The Hoopes comparison {#the-hoopes-comparison}

Jeffrey Hoopes, "Galle v Rauh: Comparing Two Revenue Estimates for California Billionaire
Taxation" (SSRN 6428578), is the one published side-by-side of the two estimates. His
Figure 2 (p.6) is a waterfall from the "Galle estimate" to "Rauh net fiscal effect". It
prints no values, so his column below is read off the chart
(`comparison/tools/digitize_hoopes_fig2.py`, tick fit within
`r usd(as.numeric(k$hoopes$tick_fit_max_resid[1]), 1)`). Beside it is the bridge read in his
order. The overview page lists every difference between the two in its Hoopes section.

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("the Hoopes comparison", "build_all")
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
hz <- ex$hoopes
scroll(show(data.frame(
  `Hoopes Figure 2 bar` = {lab <- k$hoopes$step_label[match(hz$step_id, k$hoopes$step_id)]; ifelse(is.na(lab), "(no bar)", lab)},
  `Hoopes (read off the chart)` = ifelse(is.na(hz$hoopes), "none",
    paste0(vapply(hz$hoopes, function(x) if (is.na(x)) "" else money(x, 1, TRUE), "") |>
             replace(hz$step_id == "galle_estimate", money(hz$hoopes[hz$step_id == "galle_estimate"], 1)),
           ifelse(is.na(hz$hoopes_uncertainty), "", paste0(" &plusmn; ", formatC(hz$hoopes_uncertainty, format = "f", digits = 1))))),
  `Ours, one order` = vapply(seq_along(hz$ours), function(i) { x <- hz$ours[i]
    if (is.na(x)) "none" else money(x, if (abs(x) < 0.05) 4 else 1, hz$step_id[i] != "galle_estimate") }, ""),
  `Our steps` = esc(hz$our_steps), check.names = FALSE)))
```

# Every input, by origin {#every-input-by-origin}

The OPA framework sorts every input by where it comes from: **data** (settled by observable
facts), **research** (a published estimate), **guesswork** (asserted without data or a study
behind it) and **scenario** (a choice of which world is estimated). Each bridge step carries
one of these kinds (the tables above). The values the comparison transcribes from the PDFs
itself, because neither contract carries them, are in `comparison/data/document-inputs.csv`:

```{r}
#| results: asis
twin_fold("reading the inputs", c("read_contracts", "pick"))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
dd <- k$docs[order(k$docs$label, k$docs$side), ]
scroll(show(data.frame(
  Origin = dd$label, Side = dd$side, Input = esc(dd$description),
  Value = paste(format(dd$value, drop0trailing = TRUE), dd$unit), Source = esc(dd$source),
  check.names = FALSE)))
cnt <- table(k$docs$label)
cat(sprintf("\n%d transcribed inputs: %s.\n", nrow(k$docs),
            paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(cnt), as.integer(cnt)), collapse = ", ")))
```

# What reproduces {#what-reproduces}

```{r}
pdir <- file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "py")
py_ok <- dir.exists(pdir)
maxdiff <- if (py_ok) max(vapply(c("ends", "bridge", "endpoints"), function(f) {
  r <- read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r", paste0(f, ".csv")))
  p <- read_csv_plain(file.path(pdir, paste0(f, ".csv")))
  key <- intersect(c("horizon_setting", "output", "step_id", "endpoint_id"), names(r))
  p <- p[match(do.call(paste, r[key]), do.call(paste, p[key])), ]
  cols <- setdiff(names(r)[vapply(r, is.numeric, TRUE)], "sequential_rank")
  max(vapply(cols, function(cc) max(abs(r[[cc]] - as.numeric(p[[cc]])), na.rm = TRUE), 0))
}, 0)) else NA
```

- **Both ends.** At the all-BSZ inputs the estimating function returns BSZ Table 5 row 1
  exactly (`r usd(ea$bsz_model, 3)`). At the all-RJKDC inputs it returns the expectation of
  Rauh's SSRN Monte Carlo up to a model difference of `r usd(ea$rauh_residual, 4, TRUE)` on
  (a) and `r usd(eb$rauh_residual, 2, TRUE)` on (b), from the rounded literals in the
  authors' code. Rauh's printed `r usd(epv("rauh_ssrn_npv", "printed_value"))` is
  `r usd(eb$rauh_own, 3)` unrounded.
- **The bridge adds up.** In every horizon setting and for both outputs, the Shapley steps
  sum exactly to the distance between the two model ends (`test-shapley.R`), and they match
  a brute-force average over orders.
- **R and Python agree.** The Python twin writes the same tables;
  the largest difference on the ends, the bridge and the endpoints is
  `r if (py_ok) formatC(maxdiff, format = "e", digits = 1) else "not checked (run comparison/py/bridge.py)"`
  (`test-parity.R` requires 1e-9).
- **Not reproduced.** The comparison does not re-run either side: it takes each side's
  export contract as given, and each side's own reproduction is on its overview page.

# Reproducing this document

```sh
Rscript comparison/run.R                 # exports (R and Python) and the overview page
Rscript comparison/tests/testthat.R      # the test suite
cd comparison/site && quarto render repro.qmd
```
